results.title: Phonetic Query Expansion for Spoken Document Retrieval
results.snippet: Proposes phonetically expanding spoken queries with a joint maximum-entropy n-gram model and reports improved phonetic search performance on NIST spoken term detection data. Operates directly over phoneme sequences and n-gram phonetic modeling for search.

results.title: A Survey of Automatic Query Expansion in Information Retrieval
results.snippet: Reviews many query-expansion methods used to improve recall in information retrieval, including approaches that incorporate lexical variation, morphological decomposition, and related-term generation for wider retrieval surface.

results.title: Query Expansion in the Age of Pre-trained and Large Language Models
results.snippet: Places retrieval-augmented generation within a broader taxonomy of modern query-expansion techniques and explicitly discusses RAG-related query-expansion methods, sub-word tokenization, and their role in retrieval pipelines.

results.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation meets Theoretical Linguistics
results.snippet: Integrates theoretical linguistics into RAG systems, discussing how phonological and morphological analysis can improve retrieval quality and reduce hallucination in language model outputs.

results.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architecture
results.snippet: Comprehensive survey of RAG architectures covering retrieval mechanisms, query processing pipelines, tokenization strategies, and the role of linguistic features in improving retrieval recall and precision.
